## What's new

- **Give your agents a public voice.** Squads can set how their agents write commit messages, pull requests, review replies and comments. Ficus can draft a voice from your GitHub writing and shows its progress while it works. Voices has its own settings page, next to Agents (previously Agent Types).
- **Leftover processes are cleaned up.** Dev servers and other background processes left behind by finished agent work, or started under a capacity slot that is released or expires, are now stopped automatically, so they don't keep slowing the workspace.
- **Fairer capacity sharing.** Capacity slots can share one budget across every squad on the same host, can follow that budget instead of a fixed cap, and let long-waiting work move up the queue. Settings shows the budget each pool is using.
- **Steadier hosts under memory pressure.** Ficus Cloud hosts protect their own memory, so one busy workspace can no longer stall setup and health checks for the others.
- **A lighter web app.** An open tab now makes far fewer list requests, which keeps the app and its server responsive on busy instances.
- **Newer default models.** The Lite, Fast and Exhaustive model tiers move to the newest Claude models.
- **More precise event rules.** Event rule conditions can match labels or assignees that do *not* include a value, and GitHub and Linear labels are compared case-insensitively.
- **Smoother reviews and delivery.** Agents re-request review after fixing requested changes, answers to questions reach the delivering agent after its step ends, and the delivering agent can request rework when needed.
- **Smaller fixes.** Desktop windows stay draggable while a dialog is open, the frosted glass effect is back, interrupted server updates rebuild what they missed, and agents get leaner, more accurate guidance.
